## Maintainer request — 2026-10-11

> Also, there isn’t a way to see your connected rclone backends and remove or modify them. For example, I already linked Dropbox, but I want to connect Dropbox again. If I go through rclone setup again it isn’t clear if I’d be adding a second Dropbox remote or replacing the existing one. We need to streamline and clarify the flow, including aging management screens in EmulationStation, potentially.

## Initially observed behavior and accepted scope

The existing Cloud page provides provider setup and category-folder selection, but no clear lifecycle surface for existing connections. `cloud_oauth.Session._create_remote_locked` checks configured names and refuses to overwrite an existing name. ES1d76b3da7 openCloudAddRemote and provider search call cloudOAuthStart with backend.name; Dropbox always requests dropbox. If that exact name exists, OAuth completion refuses it. There is no automatic dropbox2 allocation or reauthorization. If the previous Dropbox connection has a different name, this can create a separate dropbox remote. A YOUR CONNECTIONS list and REPAIR A CONNECTION do exist, but behind USE A COMPUTER INSTEAD and SSH instructions; no native remove action is exposed. This is distinct from #536's pointer/click failure on Dropbox's first sign-in screen.

Build on #51's native setup and #508's qualified selected-folder contract. Preserve independently selected saves, settings-backup and content paths. Linking alone must not create folders, move files, or silently change which remote automatic sync uses. Retain single-active-remote sync policy unless explicitly reconsidered; multiple stored connections are not multi-remote sync.

D-CLOUD-183 records the requested lifecycle clarity. Exact-source trace and sanitized browser observation are retained in docs/qa-logs/2026-10-11-cloud-owner-feedback/. At initial triage the proposal below was not implemented. The current implementation status below supersedes that historical observation. The canonical menu map has stale historical version-boundary prose; reconcile it when updating the source-bound flow/frame reference.

## Accepted flow

A Cloud connections management surface lists configured connections with provider/name and usage. Selecting one exposes clear connection details and deliberate actions to sign in again, change supported settings, or remove the connection from this device. Adding another connection is a separately named action; it must say that it adds rather than replaces. Signing in again targets the existing connection and preserves its identity and selected folders. Removal explains that it removes local access, not cloud files, and handles any selected category or automatic-sync dependency before committing. Do not silently enable sync or switch accounts/paths. Exact menu placement and copy must follow the canonical ES references.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes. Synthetic configured remotes and credential-free local backends can prove existing/add/reauthorize/edit/remove, cancellation, rollback, active-reference handling, busy-operation refusal and byte preservation. OAuth lifecycle tests use stubbed disposable credentials; real provider sign-in requires a separately authorized QA account. No change to the owner's existing remote or sign-in is authorized by filing/planning this work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Exact-source trace and current UI frames establish what a second setup does, how names are allocated, which paths are selected, and what management actions exist today; distinguish stored from authenticated/reachable connections.
- [x] Canonical menu/IA/flow contract clearly separates add, use existing, sign in again, edit and remove; reviewed happy/branch frames show existing provider/account ambiguity, cancellation and actionable failures, at target sizes and supported locales where changed.
- [x] VM fixtures prove reauthorization preserves the selected remote and folders, new connection creation never overwrites another, failed/cancelled authentication leaves the prior working configuration intact, and edited identity/account changes require an explicit path/usage decision.
- [x] VM before/after manifests prove local removal leaves cloud bytes and unrelated connections intact, handles selected saves/settings/content references and automatic-sync state explicitly, and cannot race an active cloud job into an invalid configuration.
- [ ] Installed-image clean and retained-configuration tests cover this flow alongside normal backup/restore and manual folder creation; source/pin, syntax, applicable audit and exact-source screenshot evidence are recorded before completion.

Parent #344; related #51, #508, #535 and #536. Resolve the design and source changes before the next source freeze; no firmware build is started by this tracking task.


## Additional maintainer report — failed code pairing

> When the code pairing fails, the screen says that the choices are OK or exit, but while it is clear what exit would do, if OK would do something different, it isn’t clear what OK would do. Do they do the same thing? ￼

> To clarify, I mean pairing a remote via the code. Hopefully this helps specify which screen I’m talking about. ￼

Exact ES1d76b3da7 trace: cloudOAuthShowSignIn checks `status == "failed"` and creates the `THE SIGN-IN DID NOT COMPLETE... START AGAIN TO GET A NEW ONE.` dialog. OK has a null callback; GuiMsgBox::deleteMeAndCall dismisses only the dialog. EXIT closes the owning setup page, whose cloudOAuthOwnSession finalizer invokes cloud_oauth cancel. Neither action retries. Continuing from the retained failed page reaches the same failure again. These are different actions, inadequately labeled. The generic failure branch also blames expired/single-use codes without distinguishing the actual cause.

Include this in #537's lifecycle/failure design. Proposed actions: TRY AGAIN starts a fresh owned attempt and obtains fresh sign-in/code state; CANCEL SIGN-IN closes/cancels. Detect a same-name existing connection before new authentication or route it deliberately to sign-in-again, rather than looping a duplicate-name failure through retries. Use stable, sanitized cause-aware wording; never promise that a code expired when only a generic failed state is known.

Can this be done on the VM? Yes: synthetic failed/expired/duplicate-name/cancelled/superseded attempts, actual dialog callbacks and process/state receipts. No further owner screenshot or input is needed for the source explanation.

- [x] The installed failure flow has explicitly named outcomes; VM evidence proves retry starts a fresh owned attempt/code, cancellation closes and releases only its own session, old callbacks cannot overwrite the new state, and failed/duplicate-name cases preserve existing credentials/paths. EN/FR reviewed failure/retry/cancel frames and the canonical flow reflect the actual actions.

## Current implementation and audit — 2026-10-11 07:12 UTC

Native CLOUD CONNECTIONS now separates add/use/renew/edit/remove, explicitly records one active connection, preserves selected paths and rejects automatic-sync/busy changes. Private staging and rollback protect both credentials and active-selection bytes. The pairing failure dialog has actual TRY AGAIN and CANCEL SIGN-IN actions. 21 actual-guest transaction controls pass, plus source-bound lifecycle/forms/guard/retry/cancel proof; final whole-flow EN/FR640/1280 captures against ES11 are complete. All16 driver jobs ended0 at07:35:48UTC; the supervisor and watcher exited. 83 reviewed final-matrix frames plus editor/browser proof are indexed in the local feature packet, including95 schema1 evidence entries. Canonical menu/flow references link the exact-source proof. The three audit repairs below are still unresolved.

The frozen primary audit reproduced three required integration fixes, recorded in [the audit update](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/issues/537#issuecomment-6106537442): include active selection in scan identity, put folder creation under the shared transfer lock, and bind destructive previews to the account/configuration that was checked. All were reproduced using local aliases and tiny synthetic files in the disposable VM. They remain unresolved; no integration or RC claim is made.

The 893 KB sanitized external-refutation packet is prepared and awaits named transfer approval. The source remains frozen for that review. Final evidence/public-doc delivery, corrected local protocol tests and installed-image clean/retained qualification remain required. Existing owner credentials/devices/cloud content were not touched.

## Verified source delivery — 2026-10-11T16:27:55.227775+00:00

Distribution [bc2dceb406](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/commit/bc2dceb406969a401d987de168acfb3ae60b7e01) and ES [c8dc72cf9e](https://github.com/pixelelated/emulationstation/commit/c8dc72cf9ec00ab00d6c4a9fcdcea1746c6f1f78) are integrated and pushed. Final delivery head `849e8dd3126a43f53abcae2678622c75ef85a08f` has successful exact-head hosted record and private-word checks. [Canonical flow/evidence packet](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/849e8dd3126a43f53abcae2678622c75ef85a08f/docs/qa-logs/2026-10-11-network-cloud-management); [independent audit, all seven repairs and Phase7 resolution](https://github.com/pixelelated/distribution/tree/849e8dd3126a43f53abcae2678622c75ef85a08f/docs/audits/2026_10_11-epic-m7-network-cloud-344).

AC1–4/6: explicit native lifecycle and reviewed NC01–NC16 EN/FR640/1280 frames; 26 actual-rclone transaction tests, 15 full-script refusals, selection/scan/preview invalidation, seed-writer exclusion, private staging cleanup, retry/cancel lifetime controls and 108 WebDAV+108 SFTP controls. All seven #540 findings are resolved. AC5 stays OPEN: assemble the changed firmware and run clean/public ROCKNIX and retained-configuration qualification. This issue is not closed by source overlays.

Only owned VM/local synthetic endpoints were used. The source fix is delivered; no new firmware image, owner-device update or personal-cloud action is claimed. Combined-image release qualification remains under #344/#537.
